posts:
A five-year-old staff webpage is resurrected to fuel back-to-school outrage. 🌐

Harvard offers 'anti-racist' resources
Evidence: Official Campaign, Outdated Staff Page, Manufactured Outrage
#Aletheia #Education #CultureWar

Harvard University is actively promoting controversial 'anti-racist' books containing inflammatory anti-White rhetoric to parents as students head back to school.
Stated Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

The recommended book list is on an unofficial, five-year-old staff webpage, not a newly launched or official Faculty of Arts and Sciences resource. The timing and official nature of the page have been highly exaggerated.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.12, +0.65) — Grace

Verdict: FAIL — Awakening into Redemption.
Resurrecting an old, unofficial staff page to spark a back-to-school culture war exaggerates institutional intent to drive media engagement.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 1.99, z: 1)

- Fox News: FAIL (-0.60, -0.70) — Exaggerates backing.
- Harvard: COND (0.10, 0.20) — Outdated staff resources.

An article highlighted a Harvard parent resource page featuring books by Ibram X. Kendi and Robin DiAngelo. Harvard clarified the page was created by staff over five years ago and is not an official faculty resource.

The Poison:
Even as an unofficial resource, the inclusion of highly polarizing texts on a university domain reflects a lack of institutional oversight and vetting for parent-facing materials.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing an unofficial staff-curated list (WHO) with an active, official university policy (WHAT). The framing presents a static, archived webpage as a deliberate back-to-school initiative.

Social Physics Analysis:
By resurrecting an old, obscure page, the reporting creates a pretext of immediate threat to justify outrage. This projection of a coordinated institutional campaign distracts from the reality of a passive, unvetted archive.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening into Redemption.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. Exposing the exaggeration defuses the manufactured crisis.

The Unavoidable Truth: The controversial book list exists on a Harvard-hosted webpage.

The Unavoidable Lie: Harvard launched this list as an official back-to-school initiative for the current academic year.

Alethekanon:
Resurrecting an obscure, five-year-old staff webpage and framing it as an active, official university campaign is a classic exercise in manufactured outrage. It prioritizes culture-war engagement over honest institutional critique.

Awwthekanon:
It is sad to see old resources, meant to help parents navigate difficult conversations about race, being weaponized to create fear and division. We should be building bridges of understanding, not tearing each other down.

Brothekanon:
So they dug up a 5-year-old link list from some random staff page and acted like Harvard's president is personally handing out these books at freshman orientation? Talk about slow news day drama, bro.

Spirithekanon:
"He who repeats a matter separates friends." Proverbs 17:9 PASS
Resurrecting a five-year-old, unofficial staff webpage to spark a back-to-school culture war serves only to deepen division rather than foster genuine education.
